text:
alisa: Quick question — thinking about using a mediator service between clients and model-serving backends instead of a single gateway adapter. Pros/cons?

matt: mediator = small stateful routing + policy logic? curious. What's driving this?

alisa: mainly runtime routing for model variants, tenant quota binding, and more granular telemetry without overloading gateway.

ravi: inclination: gateway handles translation (proto <-> json) + auth. mediator could be used for heavy policy decisions and gradual rollout. But adds hop.

jen: concerned about latency SLOs. extra hop adds RTT and SRE overhead. Do we have numbers?

sam: we measured earlier: grpc call inside cluster ~1.5ms p50; extra hop was ~3-5ms p99 under load. still maybe ok for non-RT interactive calls.

matt: Another angle: typed errors & contract evolution. mediator can translate legacy REST clients to new protobuf surfaces and keep surface stable.

alisa: yes, and mediator could keep per-tenant quotas & circuit-breakers closer to routing logic. But how do we get telemetry into Console?

ravi: push metrics as request attributes -> control plane collects, console shows per-route token cost, latency breakdown. mediator should attach earned_headers or route_id.

jen: rollout UX: if mediator exists, canarying by route is easier: mediator decides which model variant to send. But need rollback hooks in console.

sam: sample config we sketched:
```yaml
mediator:
  routes:
    - id: classify-v2
      match: /v2/classify
      target: model-service:2180
      quota_key: tenant_id
      rollout:
        percent: 10
        fallback: classify-v1
```

matt: looks good. Who manages the proto definitions then? mediator or model-service?

alisa: prefer single source: model-service owns proto; mediator imports compiled stubs. keeps contracts collocated with implementation.

ravi: question about auth: JWT validation at edge -> pass principal to mediator via headers. DO NOT revalidate in mediator.

jen: also need consistent tracing: mediator must forward trace headers and sample tags so Console's trace view can stitch spans.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/mediator-v0.3 -> deployment/mediator (canary=10%)

sam: quick ops note: add quota metrics: 'quota.request' & 'quota.denied' with route label. console can graph and alert.

matt: last point: if we choose mediator, keep it lightweight. No heavy model logic. it's routing/policy/telemetry only.

alisa: agreed. next: I'll prototype mediator with GRPC internal-to-internal, REST edge->mediator. anyone want to pair on prototyping?

ravi: I'll help. set up spike and perf test.

jen: I can add console hooks for rollout UI and quota charts.

sam: ok grabbed. Tagging infra for capacity testing later. :thumbsup:
